component: Lazy custom-element definition wait and limits

quotes.text:
/**
 * Helper function to lazily load a custom element once it is actually used.
 * Delays loading until the document is at least interactive.
 *
 * Consider using import() whenever possible to load custom element modules
 * lazily.
 *
 * This will not load the element when using customElements.upgrade.
 *
 * While this is an async function, it is only used for better control flow of
 * the lazy definition and it is not necessary to await the promise when calling
 * this function.
 *
 * @param {string} tagName - Tag name of the custom element.
 * @param {string} moduleURI - URI of module that defines the custom element.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The helper is async for readiness/control flow, and its documentation says callers need not await it. The test calls without awaiting, creates an element, then awaits customElements.whenDefined before checking the registered factory and instanceof. That observes definition rather than assuming a completed class import from the registration call. The helper also documents that customElements.upgrade does not trigger loading and recommends direct import() when possible. Preserve those limits instead of treating it as a general async loader.
title: Wait for the definition when a test needs a lazy custom-element constructor
